title: Smash Fest! (soft-launched as "Cannon Fest")
genre: Hybrid-casual puzzle / physics 'smash puzzle' (fire colored cannonballs to shatter matching cans/jars on platforms)
release_date: Global launch early June 2026 (iOS + Android) [CONFIRMED/ESTIMATE – Gamigion and FoxData describe a June 2026 global release]; entered the US iOS top 50 in 62 markets by 2026-06-12 and the US iOS top 3 on 2026-06-15 [ESTIMATE – FoxData]
early_access_date: Soft launch Dec 2025 as 'Cannon Fest', renamed Smash Fest! in May 2026 (per caller lead – not independently re-verified; iOS app id 6748084174 suggests the store record dates from mid-2025)
window_note: in window (soft launch Dec 2025, global launch June 2026)
team_size: no data – no source found giving Flow Games' headcount (7 searches across Gamigion, FoxData, mobilegamer.biz, LinkedIn/Crunchbase-type results). Founders are described as veterans of Peak Games (and, per caller lead, Good Job Games, Dream Games, Grand Games). Unverified whether the team is 5 or fewer; a studio of ex-Peak/Dream veterans shipping a polished live-ops hybrid-casual game is likely a small professional team (probably >5 people), so do NOT treat it as a confirmed 1–5 person team.
developer_background: New studio; founders previously worked at Peak Games [ESTIMATE – Chinese trade report cited via FoxData/Baijing search results] and other Istanbul casual-game studios (Good Job Games, Dream Games, Grand Games per caller lead). The core mechanic is lifted from Peak's Toon Blast limited-time LiveOps event 'Cannon Fest' (cannonballs earned in match-3 levels used to clear objects in a separate event level), which explains both the soft-launch name and the later takedown.
platforms_and_store_links: iOS: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/smash-fest/id6748084174 ; Google Play: removed end of July 2026 (reportedly after a DMCA claim by Peak Games – Gamigion, unverified)
business_model: F2P hybrid-casual: interstitial + rewarded ads (ads start only after level 20), IAP currency/booster packs and a no-ads offer [ESTIMATE/analysis – Gamigion]
units_or_downloads: ~2.9M downloads in the first month, 66.6% from the US [ESTIMATE – FoxData]; 6.41M iOS downloads in July 2026, #1 worldwide in iOS game downloads that month (up from #6) [ESTIMATE – FoxData]; 15M+ installs by end of July 2026 [ESTIMATE – AppMagic via Gamigion] vs 14.2M (another tracker) / 14.7M by August tally; August iOS ~5–6M (FoxData: down ~18% MoM; #2 iOS downloads behind Block Out!) [ESTIMATE]; run-rate ~300k downloads/day at peak [ESTIMATE – Gamigion analysis]. Cumulative by early Oct 2026: ~20–27M [ESTIMATE – 15M by end July + ~5–6M Aug + ~4–5M Sept assumed from declining trend; iOS-only after July]. US App Store ratings: ~232k (per caller lead, not re-verified).
implied_review_multiplier: n/a (mobile). For reference: ~13M US-heavy iOS downloads vs ~232k US ratings ⇒ very roughly 40–60 downloads per US rating [ESTIMATE – rough]
gross_revenue: IAP: ~$4M by end of July 2026 (AppMagic via Gamigion) / ~$3.5M (other tracker) / ~$5M headline in a later Gamigion piece ('38 Clones, $5M Revenue') [ESTIMATE]; take ~$5–6M IAP gross by early Oct 2026 [ESTIMATE – extrapolated from declining trend]. Ads: no tracker figure found; ~$2–6M [ESTIMATE – ~20–27M installs × $0.10–$0.25 ad revenue per install to date, US-heavy, ads only after level 20]. Total gross ≈ $7–12M [ESTIMATE]. A LinkedIn commentator claimed the mechanic 'scaled to ~$500K/day' – unverified and inconsistent with tracker figures.
net_revenue: IAP net ≈ $5–6M × 0.70 (Apple/Google 30% since >$1M/yr) × 0.93 ≈ $3.3–3.9M; ad revenue has no store cut (tracker-style figures already net of ad-network share) ≈ $1.9–5.6M after ×0.93; total net ≈ $5–9M before UA spend [ESTIMATE – spec method]. UA spend: no data (see conflict on 'zero paid UA' vs AppLovin UA).
production_cost: no disclosed figure. Assumed 5–10 people × ~9–12 months (pre-soft-launch prototyping through June 2026 launch) × $3k/month ≈ $135k–$360k [ESTIMATE – spec method, Turkey rate; team size assumed, not confirmed]
development_time: ~6–12 months to global launch (soft launch Dec 2025 → global June 2026; store record from mid-2025) [ESTIMATE]
why_popular: A proven, highly satisfying LiveOps mechanic from Toon Blast extracted into a standalone game: tap to fire color-matched cannonballs and watch cans/jars shatter with physics. Needs zero explanation in a 3-second clip, delivers instant tactile 'crunch', short levels, and booster/fail-state monetization familiar from Peak/Dream-style puzzles.
marketing_channels: Organic short-form video (TikTok/Instagram Reels gameplay clips of jars shattering) cited by FoxData as the main driver – 'zero paid UA' per FoxData headline; FoxData later noted the TikTok momentum cooled in August. Conflicting view: Gamigion analysis says it scaled to ~300k downloads/day on ~50 creatives and essentially one excellent playable ad, with ~90% of spend on AppLovin – i.e. paid UA was significant. App Store chart #1 in the US (June/July) then fed further organic installs. 38–70 copycat 'smash puzzle' games followed (Royal Smash by Cypher Games, Spyke Games, etc.).
engine: no data (not disclosed; Turkish hybrid-casual studios typically use Unity – unverified)
art_style: Bright, colorful casual 2D/3D cartoon; glossy cans/jars and cannonballs with physics shatter effects
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: code the projectile/physics/stacking logic, color-matching rules, level data and a level editor, ad/IAP integration; generate colorful 2D/3D props (cans, jars, cannons), UI, SFX and music. | AI cannot: nail the physics 'crunch' and juice that makes clips go viral, balance difficulty vs boosters (Gamigion's playtest found boosters felt weak), design hundreds of levels with a good difficulty curve, run creative testing/UA, or avoid IP risk – this game was pulled from Google Play over a DMCA by Peak Games because the mechanic copied Toon Blast's Cannon Fest. | Toolset: Claude Code + Unity 6 (or Godot 4) with built-in physics, AppLovin MAX/AdMob + Unity IAP/RevenueCat, Meshy/Tripo for 3D props or Scenario for 2D, ElevenLabs SFX, Suno music, CapCut/AI video for TikTok clips.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 3–6 weeks, $200–$600 (Claude Pro/Max, 3D/2D gen subs, Apple $99/yr, Google $25; excludes living costs)
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 3–5 months, $3,000–$12,000 (tools, freelance VFX/art polish, 200+ levels, LiveOps basics, $2k–$8k UA/creative tests)

data_conflicts: 1) Paid UA: FoxData headline says 'zero paid UA' and credits organic TikTok/Reels; Gamigion analysis says it scaled via ~50 creatives and one playable, ~90% on AppLovin – reported both; organic virality likely started it, paid UA likely amplified it. 2) Downloads: 15M+ by end July (AppMagic) vs 14.2M / 14.7M (other trackers/dates). 3) IAP revenue: $3.5M vs $4M vs $5M headline – different dates/trackers; used a $5–6M range for early Oct. 4) LinkedIn claim of ~$500K/day is far above tracker figures – treated as unreliable. 5) Team size and the 'veterans of Good Job/Peak/Dream/Grand' detail: only Peak Games background found in search results; headcount unknown. 6) Soft-launch timeline (Dec 2025 as Cannon Fest, renamed May 2026) comes from the caller's lead; the iOS id (6748084174) points to a store record created around mid-2025.
notes: Key lesson: the hook was a proven mechanic hidden inside a top-grossing game's LiveOps event, extracted into a standalone game and shown in 3-second, instantly readable clips. But the IP risk was real: the game was pulled from Google Play (reportedly a DMCA by Peak Games) right as it peaked, and dozens of clones (Royal Smash ~7–9M installs) eroded it within weeks. A solo creator can prototype this kind of 'satisfying physics clip' game quickly, but should take inspiration from public-domain mechanics, build a differentiating twist, and move fast on iOS + Android at once. Not confirmed as a 1–5 person team.
